about: Language setup for devops-multi-agent-team. The installer, the mod and the MCP server read this file; LANGUAGES.md explains it. Layers are sorting tags only: every language can be set up for any purpose. Add a language by appending an entry, by chat through the MCP server, or per project in .devops/languages.local.json (merged by id).

web.summary: Runs in a browser or webview: UI, styles, client state.

backend.summary: Services, APIs, workers, data access, business rules.

systems.summary: Native code, kernels, drivers, FFI libraries, anything with manual memory or an ABI.

scripting.summary: Glue: dev stack scripts, build helpers, checks, automation.

infra.summary: Pipelines, containers, IaC, deploy and environment config.

game.summary: Game engines, game logic and the scripting that drives them. A tag for sorting, not a restriction: any language here can do anything.

science.summary: Data science, numerical and functional-first work. A tag for sorting, not a restriction.

languages.name: C

install: apt-get install -y build-essential clang clang-tidy cppcheck

validate: <project build, e.g. make | cmake --build build | meson compile -C build>
<project tests, e.g. make test | ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure>
build once with -Wall -Wextra -Werror and once with -fsanitize=address,undefined
style: Follow the project's .clang-format; do not reflow unrelated lines.
sensitiveHints: allocators, locking, parsing of untrusted bytes, path and permission checks, syscalls

interactsWith.via: calling convention; the assembly layer owns primitives, C owns policy

interactsWith.contract: the generated header and an ABI version constant

setupNotes: Memory primitives, allocator internals, low-level synchronization and port I/O belong in the architecture-specific ASM layer; C holds policy, orchestration and services.
Frozen contract and ABI headers are wire/ABI: append, never renumber or reorder.
If a make target needs a cross compiler or emcc that is not installed, report NOT RUN, never a pass.

docs.format: Doxygen comments (/** … */ or ///) on public functions, structs and headers
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: doxygen with WARN_AS_ERROR=YES (or clang -Wdocumentation)

languages.name: C++

install: apt-get install -y build-essential clang clang-tidy clang-format cmake ninja-build

validate: rebuild with -fsanitize=address,undefined (and thread for concurrent code)
style: Follow the project's .clang-format and .clang-tidy; prefer RAII and std types over manual memory.
sensitiveHints: raw owning pointers, unsafe casts, lifetime of views, deserialization

interactsWith.contract: exported C ABI plus a managed wrapper
the binding module and its stubs

setupNotes: One CodeQL language id (cpp) covers C and C++; run it once with the project's build command.
Unreal Engine C++ builds with UnrealBuildTool and the engine installed; that is NOT RUN in the sandbox. Engine-independent game logic can be built with CMake as usual.

docs.format: Doxygen comments on public classes and functions
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: doxygen with WARN_AS_ERROR=YES (or clang -Wdocumentation)

languages.name: Assembly
validate: assemble every changed file for each supported architecture (as / nasm / cross as)
run the C and ASM interop tests the project defines
objdump -d <object> and compare the changed symbols with their C declarations

security.note: No scanner reads assembly. The Security seat reviews it by hand and the report says so.

style: Keep one architecture per directory; name every global symbol with the project prefix; comment the calling convention at the top of each routine.
sensitiveHints: stack and register discipline, privileged instructions, port I/O, atomics and locks
setupNotes: Do not mix GAS and NASM syntax in one tree unless the build already does; keep the dialect the directory uses.
A change that touches assembly always takes the full gate: reviewers cannot lean on a scanner.
The gcc image carries GNU as; install nasm in your own pinned image if the tree uses NASM.

docs.format: a header comment per routine stating the calling convention, inputs, outputs and clobbered registers (not recoverable from the code)
docs.lineComment: ; (GAS on x86 uses # or /* */; NASM uses ;)
docs.check: none: reviewed by hand

languages.name: Rust

install: rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown   # only if the project builds wasm

validate: cargo build --locked --features <each feature set the project ships, e.g. provider>
style: rustfmt defaults unless the repo has rustfmt.toml.
Tests live in their own file next to the module (src/<module>/tests.rs or #[path]), not in an inline #[cfg(test)] module in the implementation file.
Tests never write a secret as a literal; draw passphrases, PINs and nonces at run time from one test-secrets helper.
Secrets are Zeroizing<..>; a test's assertion message never formats a Result, error or output that could hold one.
sensitiveHints: unsafe blocks, FFI exports, key derivation, encryption, signature and quorum checks, any #[no_mangle]

interactsWith.via: wasm32 build (wasm-bindgen / worker crate) loaded by the frontend or a Worker
interactsWith.contract: the generated .d.ts and a wasm build script; features that cannot combine are refused in build.rs
the header plus an ABI version constant; one archive carries all headers

interactsWith.via: deploy of the Worker or service

setupNotes: Run the lint and test lines with --features for every shipped combination; a build that is clean without a feature can be broken with it.
Wire-format codes, kind bytes and event codes are append-only; the review fails a renumbering.
A feature that must not coexist (for example a provider host and the wasm lab) is refused in build.rs; keep that guard when adding features.

docs.format: rustdoc: /// on items, //! on modules and crates, with # Errors, # Panics and # Safety sections where they apply
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --no-deps; #![warn(missing_docs)] for libraries

languages.name: Go

install: install Go from https://go.dev/dl (match go.mod's go directive)

style: gofmt is law; exported names carry doc comments; errors are wrapped with %w, never swallowed.
sensitiveHints: net/http handlers, template/exec use, crypto/*, unsafe, goroutine leaks and shared state
setupNotes: Run go test -race for any change touching goroutines or shared state.

docs.format: godoc: when a comment is warranted, put it directly above the name and start it with the name
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: go vet; staticcheck (ST1000 family); revive exported rule

languages.name: C# / .NET

install: install the .NET SDK named in global.json (https://dot.net)

style: Match the project's naming, primary constructors and file-scoped namespaces; .editorconfig is the authority.
Prefer pattern matching (switch expressions, property/relational patterns) over long if/else chains for closed-set decisions.

optInStyle.rule: No `var` and no `dynamic`: write explicit types for locals, foreach variables and pattern positions; pin it with csharp_style_var_* = false:error in .editorconfig and EnforceCodeStyleInBuild so a green build proves it. Do not even write the bare word var in prose.

sensitiveHints: authentication and authorization attributes, EF raw SQL, deserialization, file uploads, process start, SignalR hub methods

interactsWith.via: REST/JSON and SignalR to the SPA
interactsWith.contract: OpenAPI or a shared DTO file; the client types are regenerated or updated in the same change
the migration set; raw SQL must be parameterized

setupNotes: CI rejects unparameterized raw SQL (FromSqlRaw / ExecuteSqlRaw / SqlQueryRaw); the Security seat greps for them every review.
Comment and documentation rules (when to comment, XML docs) belong in the project's own guide; the profile links it.
ASP.NET services and Unity/Godot-C# game code are all this entry; Unity needs the editor's own batchmode runner, which is NOT RUN in the sandbox.

docs.format: XML documentation (/// <summary>, <param>, <returns>, <exception>)
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: <GenerateDocumentationFile>true</GenerateDocumentationFile> with CS1591 as an error for public APIs

languages.name: Java

install: install a JDK matching the build's toolchain (https://adoptium.net)
use ./gradlew or ./mvnw, not a global tool

style: Follow the configured formatter (spotless/checkstyle); no wildcard imports unless the project uses them.
sensitiveHints: deserialization, JNDI/reflection, SQL string building, XML parsers (XXE), Spring security config
setupNotes: Java and Kotlin share the CodeQL id java-kotlin; run it once.

docs.format: Javadoc (/** … */ with @param, @return, @throws)
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: javadoc -Xdoclint:all

languages.name: Kotlin
style: ktlint/detekt rules from the repo; no !! on values that come from outside.
sensitiveHints: same as Java; coroutine cancellation and shared mutable state
setupNotes: Android modules need the Android SDK and the project's Gradle properties; report NOT RUN rather than guess.

docs.format: KDoc (/** … */ with @param, @return, @throws)
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: dokka; detekt UndocumentedPublicClass/Function

languages.name: Python

install: pip install ruff mypy pytest pip-audit bandit

style: ruff/black defaults unless the repo pins others; type-hint public functions; no bare except.
sensitiveHints: subprocess with shell=True, pickle/yaml.load, eval/exec, SQL string building, path joins from user input

interactsWith.contract: documented CLI flags and exit codes

setupNotes: As a backend, use the full gate; as a script, keep it small and let ruff + a smoke run be the validation.
Run untrusted checkouts with `python -I` so a planted module in the current directory is not imported.

docs.format: PEP 257 docstrings in triple quotes (Google or NumPy style, one style per project)
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: ruff check --select D (pydocstyle rules) or pydocstyle

languages.name: TypeScript

install: npm ci   (use the lockfile's package manager: pnpm/yarn if present)

style: Use const, or let when reassigned; never var. Pin no-var and prefer-const as errors in eslint.config.js and run lint with --no-inline-config so a disable comment cannot hide them.
No any unless the line says why; no innerHTML; no absolute paths in code that is mounted under a prefix.
sensitiveHints: dangerouslySetInnerHTML/innerHTML, eval, postMessage origins, auth token storage, CORS, anything parsing a server reply

interactsWith.contract: OpenAPI or shared DTOs; change both sides in one item
generated .d.ts and the wasm build script

setupNotes: One CodeQL id (javascript-typescript) covers JS and TS; `--language=javascript` also works on older CLIs.
Run commands from the package that owns them (frontend/, lab/, workers/); a monorepo has one lockfile per package.
A browser app is verified by the Verifier seat's smoke run, not by unit tests alone.

docs.format: TSDoc/JSDoc (/** … */ with @param, @returns, @throws)
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: eslint-plugin-jsdoc or eslint-plugin-tsdoc; typedoc --treatWarningsAsErrors

languages.name: JavaScript
validate: node --test   (for projects using the built-in runner)
style: const or let, never var; ES modules unless the package says otherwise; no innerHTML.
sensitiveHints: same as TypeScript; Worker/edge handlers that read request headers and bodies

interactsWith.contract: the wasm build script and its generated glue

setupNotes: Edge/Worker code (Cloudflare Workers and similar) has its own guard scripts and wrangler config: run them as part of validation and never put credentials in wrangler.toml [vars].

docs.format: JSDoc (/** … */ with @param, @returns, @throws)
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: eslint-plugin-jsdoc

languages.name: CSS / SCSS
validate: run the frontend build and the Verifier smoke in light and dark themes

security.note: Low risk; the review looks for url() with untrusted input and for leaked internal hostnames.

style: Use the project's design tokens (custom properties); do not hardcode colors, shadows or timings.

optInStyle.rule: Plain CSS with custom properties, no Tailwind, no CSS-in-JS; every visual value traces to a token in design.md; styling changes stay separate from component-structure changes.

setupNotes: Read the design doc before touching color, spacing or animation.

docs.format: a short comment above a section or hack when the reason is not clear
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: stylelint (comment-empty-line-before)

languages.name: Shell (bash/sh)
validate: run the script once with its documented flags in a throwaway directory

security.note: CodeQL does not read shell scripts. The Security seat reviews quoting, eval, temp files, PATH and curl|sh by hand and says so.

style: set -euo pipefail; quote every expansion; pass untrusted text as an argument, never inside a command string; mktemp for temp files; no predictable /tmp names.
sensitiveHints: eval, unquoted expansions, curl | sh, rm -rf with a variable, sudo, writing under /tmp

interactsWith.contract: one documented flag set and the same exit codes in both
documented CLI flags and exit codes

setupNotes: Keep scripts non-interactive and idempotent; the dev-stack scripts (run-dev.sh and run-dev.ps1) must stay in step.
Backstop scripts that grep for banned constructs (check-no-var.sh style) are CI code: a change to one takes the full gate.
The shellcheck image is enough for linting; bash -n and a real run need a bash image of your own.

docs.format: a header comment with purpose, usage and exit codes (a script's interface); comments on non-obvious options
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: shellcheck; shfmt -d

languages.name: PowerShell
validate: run the script once with its documented flags in a throwaway directory

security.note: No CodeQL support; review Invoke-Expression, -ExecutionPolicy Bypass, and string-built commands by hand.

style: Set-StrictMode -Version Latest; $ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'; use approved verbs; splat long argument lists.
sensitiveHints: Invoke-Expression, Start-Process with built strings, downloaded scripts, credentials in plain text
setupNotes: Keep the .ps1 and .sh twins of a dev script in the same change.

docs.format: comment-based help (.SYNOPSIS, .DESCRIPTION, .PARAMETER, .EXAMPLE) on functions users call directly
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: PSScriptAnalyzer rule PSProvideCommentHelp

languages.name: SQL / migrations

install: the project's migration tool (dotnet ef, sqlx, alembic, flyway, ...)

validate: apply the migration to an empty database, then to a copy with data, then roll back if reversible
run the data-access tests against the migrated schema

security.note: The analyser for the host language catches injection in code; SQL files are reviewed by hand for grants, defaults and data loss.

style: Parameterize every value; no string-built SQL; migrations are append-only and never edited after merge.
sensitiveHints: DROP/TRUNCATE/ALTER on populated tables, GRANT, default values on non-null columns, long locks

interactsWith.contract: SCHEMA_VERSION and a refusal of newer databases

setupNotes: A schema change is a wire/storage change: the review asks for the migration, the rollback story and the old-database test.

docs.format: a comment on each non-obvious query or migration step naming the reason; COMMENT ON for tables and columns where the engine supports it
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: sqlfluff

languages.name: Terraform / HCL

install: install Terraform at the version in .terraform-version / required_version
brew install tflint; pip install checkov

style: Providers pinned by .terraform.lock.hcl; no secrets in tfvars or state committed; the operator runs apply with their own credentials.
sensitiveHints: IAM and Access policies, public bucket/route exposure, rate limits and WAF rules, state backends
setupNotes: Never run apply from a seat; a plan is evidence, an apply is the operator's decision.

docs.format: a description on variables and outputs whose purpose is not clear from the name (module consumers see it); comments only for why
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: terraform-docs; tflint terraform_documented_variables / outputs

languages.name: Containers (Docker, Compose, Kubernetes, Helm)

install: brew install hadolint kubeconform helm trivy

style: Pin base images by digest; run as a non-root user; no secrets in layers, ARG or ENV; multi-stage builds.
sensitiveHints: privileged containers, hostPath mounts, latest tags, secrets in env, exposed ports
setupNotes: Some projects ship no container on purpose; do not add one without a plan.
No sandbox image: building images needs a container engine, and a container engine is never mounted into the sandbox. Run image builds on the host or in a VM with the human's OK.

docs.format: a comment above each non-obvious instruction (why this base image, why this flag)
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: hadolint

languages.name: CI workflows (GitHub Actions, Buildkite, GitLab)

install: brew install actionlint   (or download from github.com/rhysd/actionlint)

validate: check every `uses:` is pinned to a full commit SHA (or an accepted tag) and `permissions:` is least-privilege
style: Never echo secrets; pass untrusted text (PR titles, branch names) through env, not inline `${{ }}` in run:; a deploy credential is no broader than the job needs.
sensitiveHints: pull_request_target, workflow_run, self-hosted runners, write permissions, third-party actions

interactsWith.contract: the stable check name a branch rule requires

setupNotes: A required check keeps one stable name (for example `test`); a change to a workflow file always takes the full gate and is never review-bot exempt.

docs.format: a name on every workflow, job and step (needed for readable runs); comments only for why a permission or pin exists
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: actionlint

languages.name: HTML
validate: run the accessibility check the project uses (axe or pa11y) in the Verifier smoke
check links on the built site (linkinator or the framework's own)

security.note: No scanner reads this language; the Security seat reviews it by hand and the report says so.

style: Semantic elements, one h1 per page, alt text on every image, no inline event handlers or inline scripts when a CSP is set.
sensitiveHints: inline <script>, user content rendered without escaping, forms posting to external hosts, target=_blank without rel=noopener

interactsWith.contract: a documented list of hooks; tests select by role, not by class

setupNotes: Templates in a server framework (Blade, ERB, Razor, Jinja) are reviewed as that language for injection and as HTML for structure.
Set a Content-Security-Policy and test that it still allows the page to work.

docs.format: comments only for non-obvious structure or a required workaround; never commented-out markup
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: html-validate

languages.name: PHP
style: PSR-12; declare(strict_types=1) in every file; typed properties and return types; no @-suppression.
sensitiveHints: unserialize, include/require with variables, eval, exec/system/shell_exec, SQL built by concatenation, file uploads, extract() on request data

interactsWith.contract: the migration set; prepared statements only

setupNotes: Laravel and Symfony have their own console test and lint commands; put them in the profile instead of guessing.
Run composer with --no-scripts when inspecting an untrusted checkout.

docs.format: PHPDoc (/** … */ with @param, @return, @throws)
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: phpcs with the PEAR/PSR-5 doc sniffs, or phpstan

languages.name: Ruby

install: install Ruby with rbenv or asdf per .ruby-version

style: rubocop config from the repo; frozen_string_literal comment; no monkey patching of core classes.
sensitiveHints: eval, send with user input, YAML.load, system/backticks, mass assignment, raw SQL fragments
setupNotes: Rails: run db:migrate on an empty and a populated database before sign-off.
Gem versions are pinned by Gemfile.lock; a lockfile change is a dependency change.

docs.format: YARD (# @param, @return, @raise)
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: yard stats --list-undoc; rubocop Style/Documentation

languages.name: Dart / Flutter

install: install the Dart or Flutter SDK per pubspec environment (https://dart.dev, https://flutter.dev)

security.note: No scanner reads this language; the Security seat reviews it by hand and the report says so.

style: Effective Dart; analysis_options.yaml from the repo; null safety on; no dynamic without a comment.
sensitiveHints: platform channels, WebView content, local storage of tokens, http without certificate checks

interactsWith.via: Flutter web embedding or a shared API

setupNotes: Flutter device and integration tests need an emulator or device: NOT RUN in the sandbox.
Flutter needs its own SDK image; the dart image covers pure Dart packages.

docs.format: dartdoc: /// comments, first line a one-sentence summary, where the contract is not obvious
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: dart doc; public_member_api_docs lint

languages.name: Scala

install: install a JDK, then Coursier: cs setup (https://get-coursier.io)

security.note: No scanner reads this language; the Security seat reviews it by hand and the report says so.

style: scalafmt config from the repo; no null, no var in domain code, exhaustive matches.
sensitiveHints: Java deserialization, reflection, SQL interpolation, Akka/Pekko remoting config
setupNotes: No official sbt image is pinned here: build a project image from eclipse-temurin with sbt and pin its digest, or run on the host with the human's OK.
Spark jobs need a cluster or local[*] session; keep tests on local mode.

docs.format: Scaladoc (/** … */ with @param, @return, @throws)
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: sbt doc with -Xfatal-warnings

languages.name: Swift

install: install Swift (https://swift.org/install) or Xcode on macOS

style: swift-format and SwiftLint configs from the repo; prefer value types; no force unwraps outside tests.
sensitiveHints: Keychain use, App Transport Security exceptions, URL scheme handlers, unsafe pointers
setupNotes: CodeQL for Swift needs macOS; the Linux image builds Foundation-only packages. UIKit/SwiftUI/Xcode builds are NOT RUN in the sandbox.
Objective-C code in a mixed project is reviewed under this entry; it has no entry of its own.

docs.format: DocC / Swift markup: /// with - Parameter:, - Returns:, - Throws:
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: swift package generate-documentation; SwiftLint missing_docs

languages.name: Perl

security.note: No scanner reads this language; the Security seat reviews it by hand and the report says so.

style: use strict; use warnings; in every file; three-argument open; no bareword filehandles.
sensitiveHints: two-argument open, backticks and system with interpolation, eval of strings, taint-mode bypass
setupNotes: Legacy scripts often lack tests: add a characterization test (run on sample input, compare output) before changing one.

docs.format: POD (=head1, =head2, =item) in or after the code
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: podchecker; Perl::Critic Documentation policies

languages.name: Lua

install: install Lua 5.4 or LuaJIT and luarocks

security.note: No scanner reads this language; the Security seat reviews it by hand and the report says so.

style: luacheck config from the repo; local by default, no accidental globals; stylua formatting.
sensitiveHints: load/loadstring/dofile on external text, os.execute/io.popen, sandbox escapes in embedded scripts

interactsWith.via: embedding through the Lua C API
interactsWith.contract: the registered function table and its argument checks

setupNotes: For scripts embedded in a host (game engine, Neovim, nginx) the host binary is needed to run real tests: NOT RUN unless a headless mode exists.
No official image is pinned here; use the host's own CI image or a pinned custom one.

docs.format: LDoc (--- with @param, @return)
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: ldoc

languages.name: GDScript (Godot)

install: download Godot 4.x (headless/Linux) from https://godotengine.org/download and put it on PATH as godot

validate: godot --headless --path . -s addons/gut/gut_cmdln.gd -gexit   (GUT; or the GdUnit4 runner)

security.note: No scanner reads this language; the Security seat reviews it by hand and the report says so.

style: gdformat and gdlint defaults; static typing on (typed vars and returns); signals over polling.
sensitiveHints: loading user-supplied scenes/resources (they can run code), OS.execute, network peers trusted by default

interactsWith.via: Godot C# in the same project

setupNotes: Exports (Windows, Android, web) need export templates and are NOT RUN in the sandbox.
Pin the Godot version in the project and in CI: scene and resource formats change between minor versions.

docs.format: ## doc comments above classes, signals, exports and functions
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: gdlint

languages.name: Zig

install: install Zig from https://ziglang.org/download (match build.zig.zon minimum_zig_version)

security.note: No scanner reads this language; the Security seat reviews it by hand and the report says so.

style: zig fmt is law; errors are returned, not swallowed; allocators are passed in.
sensitiveHints: allocator lifetime, @ptrCast/@intFromPtr, unchecked slices in ReleaseFast, C interop

interactsWith.contract: the header and an ABI version constant

setupNotes: Zig is pre-1.0: pin the compiler version in the profile and in CI.
No official container image exists; use a pinned custom image.

docs.format: /// doc comments on declarations and //! on modules
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: zig build-lib -femit-docs

languages.name: WebAssembly
validate: wasm-opt <in>.wasm -O2 -o <out>.wasm   (binaryen; compare size and run tests after)
run the module's tests under the project's runtime (wasmtime, or node)

security.note: No scanner reads this language; the Security seat reviews it by hand and the report says so.

style: Export only what callers need; document every import and export in one file; keep the memory limit explicit.
sensitiveHints: host imports that touch files or the network (WASI capabilities), memory growth, untrusted modules

interactsWith.contract: the generated .d.ts and the build script
exports list and the JS glue
exports list and the JS glue

setupNotes: This entry is a build target, not a source language: the source language's own entry decides compile, lint and scan; here you validate the binary and its surface.
emcc and wasm-pack are usually missing in a plain sandbox: report NOT RUN rather than a pass.

docs.format: ;; comments on imports and exports whose contract the host must know
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: wasm-tools validate

languages.name: Fortran

security.note: No scanner reads this language; the Security seat reviews it by hand and the report says so.

style: implicit none everywhere; explicit kinds (iso_fortran_env); free-form source.
sensitiveHints: array bounds, integer overflow, interoperability with C pointers

interactsWith.contract: the wrapper and a tested example call
the C header and kind mappings

setupNotes: The gcc image carries gfortran but not fpm: add fpm in a pinned project image.
Numerical results are compared with a tolerance, never for equality.

docs.format: FORD-style !> doc comments before procedures and modules
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: ford

languages.name: COBOL

install: install GnuCOBOL (cobc): apt-get install gnucobol, brew install gnucobol

validate: run the program with a fixed input file and compare the output file byte for byte

security.note: No scanner reads this language; the Security seat reviews it by hand and the report says so.

style: Fixed or free format as the tree already uses; copybooks for every shared record layout; no GO TO in new code.
sensitiveHints: file record layouts (silent truncation), packed decimal handling, JCL/batch credentials, embedded SQL

interactsWith.via: batch files or MQ messages exchanged with services
interactsWith.contract: the record layout in a copybook plus a Java mapping test

setupNotes: GnuCOBOL is the free compiler; mainframe-only dialect features may not compile there: report NOT RUN for those, never a pass.
Treat a record layout like a wire format: append, never renumber or resize.

docs.format: a short comment block at the top of each program naming its purpose, inputs, outputs and return codes where the code does not make them plain
docs.check: none: reviewed by hand

languages.name: R

security.note: No scanner reads this language; the Security seat reviews it by hand and the report says so.

style: tidyverse style via styler/lintr; set seeds in every stochastic test; no setwd in packages.
sensitiveHints: system()/shell(), eval(parse()), loading .RData/.rds from untrusted sources, Shiny inputs reaching queries
setupNotes: Notebooks (.Rmd) are code: render them in CI and diff the outputs only when they are deterministic.
renv.lock is the dependency record; a change to it is a dependency change.

docs.format: roxygen2 (#' with @param, @return, @export, @examples)
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: devtools::document(); R CMD check (undocumented arguments)

languages.name: Julia
validate: julia --project -e 'using JuliaFormatter; format("."; verbose=true)' then git diff --exit-code
run Aqua.jl and JET.jl checks if the project has them

security.note: No scanner reads this language; the Security seat reviews it by hand and the report says so.

style: JuliaFormatter config from the repo; type-stable hot paths; no type piracy.
sensitiveHints: eval/include on external text, ccall signatures, shelling out

interactsWith.contract: the C header and symbol list

setupNotes: Precompilation makes the first run slow; cache ~/.julia in CI, not in the sandbox image.
Manifest.toml is committed for applications and not for libraries.

docs.format: docstrings in triple quotes above the definition, with a signature, Arguments and Examples
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: Documenter.jl doctests

languages.name: Haskell

security.note: No scanner reads this language; the Security seat reviews it by hand and the report says so.

style: -Wall -Werror in CI; ormolu or fourmolu formatting from the repo; total functions, no partial head/fromJust.
sensitiveHints: unsafePerformIO, FFI imports, Template Haskell reading files, deserialization
setupNotes: Pin GHC and the package set (stack resolver or cabal freeze file) in the profile.
First builds take long; cache dist-newstyle outside the sandbox image.

docs.format: Haddock (-- | on the line above, -- ^ after a field)
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: cabal haddock

languages.name: OCaml

install: install opam (https://opam.ocaml.org), then opam switch create . --deps-only

security.note: No scanner reads this language; the Security seat reviews it by hand and the report says so.

style: ocamlformat config from the repo; .mli for every public module; exhaustive matches with no catch-all on variants you own.
sensitiveHints: Obj.magic, Marshal on untrusted data, C stubs, unsafe array/string access

interactsWith.contract: the stub file and its tests

setupNotes: The opam image is large: pin the tag and cache switches outside the sandbox.

docs.format: odoc comments (** … *) in the .mli where a value's contract is not obvious from its type
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: dune build @doc

languages.name: Erlang

security.note: No scanner reads this language; the Security seat reviews it by hand and the report says so.

style: erlfmt formatting; specs on exported functions; supervise every long-lived process.
sensitiveHints: binary_to_term on untrusted data, os:cmd, distribution cookies and exposed epmd, ETS with public access

interactsWith.contract: a shared OTP release and module/function names
the NIF header and failure behavior (a crash takes the VM down)

setupNotes: Dialyzer is a type checker, not a security scanner; it does not change the unanalysed note.
Distributed nodes need a secret cookie from the environment, never from the repo.

docs.format: edoc (%% @doc, @param, @returns) where useful, and -spec on exported functions (specs are code, not comments)
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: rebar3 edoc; dialyzer for specs

languages.name: Elixir

install: install Elixir/OTP via asdf or the official installer (https://elixir-lang.org/install.html)

style: mix format; @spec on public functions; pattern match in function heads; let it crash under a supervisor.
sensitiveHints: String.to_atom on input, Code.eval_*, raw Ecto fragments, Phoenix params reaching queries, :erlang.binary_to_term

interactsWith.contract: module and function names; OTP release

setupNotes: Sobelow covers Phoenix apps; plain OTP libraries have no scanner, so say so in the report.

docs.format: @moduledoc and @doc with iex> doctests where the behaviour is not obvious, and @spec on public functions (specs are code)
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: mix docs; credo Readability.ModuleDoc; ExUnit doctests

languages.name: Clojure / ClojureScript

install: install the Clojure CLI (https://clojure.org/guides/install_clojure) or Leiningen

security.note: No scanner reads this language; the Security seat reviews it by hand and the report says so.

style: cljfmt and clj-kondo configs from the repo; data over macros; pure functions at the edges.
sensitiveHints: read-string/eval on external text, Java interop reflection, SQL string building

interactsWith.contract: the Java API called and its version
the shadow-cljs/cljs build config and npm deps

setupNotes: Other Lisps (Common Lisp, Scheme, Racket) are not separate entries: use this one for REPL-driven workflow notes and add a local entry if you need their toolchains.

docs.format: docstrings as the first element of def, defn and ns
docs.check: only if the project publishes API docs: clj-kondo missing-docstring linter

languages.name: F#

security.note: No scanner reads this language; the Security seat reviews it by hand and the report says so.

style: Fantomas formatting; warnings as errors; avoid null at module boundaries; make illegal states unrepresentable.
sensitiveHints: System.Diagnostics.Process, Reflection, unsafe serializers (BinaryFormatter), raw SQL strings
setupNotes: CodeQL does not support F#; the C# entry's scan covers only C# projects in the same solution.

docs.format: XML documentation (/// <summary> …)

languages.name: Lean 4

install: install elan, the Lean toolchain manager (https://github.com/leanprover/elan); the project's lean-toolchain file pins the version

validate: lake test   (only if the project defines a test driver)

security.note: No scanner reads this language and a lakefile is code that runs at build time; the Security seat reviews lakefiles and dependency revisions in lake-manifest.json by hand and the report says so.

style: Follow Mathlib style when the project depends on Mathlib; theorem and lemma names state what they prove; no sorry or admit in merged code (a proof is either done or not claimed); prefer small lemmas over one long tactic block.
sensitiveHints: lakefile.lean (arbitrary code at build), @[extern] and @[implemented_by] (code that the proof does not cover), unsafe declarations, IO actions reading the network or files

interactsWith.via: Lean compiles to C; @[extern] and @[export] cross the C ABI
interactsWith.contract: the C header and the exported symbol names

interactsWith.via: the compiled C library called through ctypes or cffi
interactsWith.contract: the C signatures; a proof about the Lean code does not cover the Python caller

interactsWith.via: the compiled C library called through JNI or the Foreign Function & Memory API
interactsWith.contract: the C signatures; a proof about the Lean code does not cover the Java caller

setupNotes: Lean 4 has no official backend for Python or Java: it emits C. A proof is evidence about the Lean model; the code in the target language still needs its own tests (see references/formal-check.md).
lake fetches dependencies over the network; run it in the sandbox with network only for the hosts the profile allows, and pin Mathlib by revision.
Mathlib builds are large: use its cache (lake exe cache get) outside the sandbox image.

docs.format: doc comments (/-- ... -/ before a declaration, /-! ... -/ for a module)
docs.check: only if the project publishes docs: the doc-gen4 dependency

rules: Prefer pattern matching (switch expressions, match, case) over long if/else chains for closed-set decisions.
Prefer fail-first control flow: validate and return or throw early, and keep the happy path unindented at the end of the function.
Prefer speakable names: rename abbreviations that cannot be said as words; conventional short forms (loop indices, ct for a cancellation token) are fine.

Prefer collection transforms (map/filter/reduce, LINQ Select/Where/Aggregate, iterator chains) when clearer; filter before looping over a subset; use explicit loops for multi-step side effects or performance-critical code.
Split functions with high cognitive complexity or deep nesting into cohesive subfunctions.
Name explicit types where the language allows implicit ones, when the project chooses (see the language's explicit-types preset).
Never silence a style or analysis rule to get green: no pragma/disable comments, NoWarn, SuppressMessage, nested config overrides or inline-config toggles for a rule the project pins as an error.
Back the pinned rules with a grep backstop script in CI (for example a check-no-var script) and run linters with inline config disabled, so a suppression cannot hide a violation.

codeqlNotes: Set DB and SARIF to paths outside the repository (a temp directory); databases and SARIF never land in git.

A CodeQL result is 'satisfied' only when: the database was created for the affected language; the analysis completed; the SARIF was read; no unresolved finding introduced or materially affected by the change remains; and no query, path filter or workflow was weakened to get there.

Run CodeQL for every affected language, and always for changes to authentication, secrets, cryptography, HTTP handling, SQL/ORM, file uploads, command execution, deserialization, XSS/SSRF surfaces and security configuration.
Unaffected languages may be NOT APPLICABLE when CI does not require all of them.
docsNote: Doc formats apply only where a doc comment is warranted: when the contract is not obvious from the name and signature, or when the project publishes generated API docs. Self-explanatory code gets no comment, and no comment is added just because code was added.
